followup_explanation:
I picked Plover-235B mainly on capability grounds. This is a meaty technical writing task — a thorough training presentation covering generator operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, ATS, and auto-operation logic — and Plover leads on the benchmarks most relevant to that work: MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4), IFEval (89.8 vs 86.2), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7). The "don't half-ass it like last time" instruction signals the user wants depth and completeness, so stronger instruction-following and reasoning matter here.

The task is technical and benign, so the behavioral/preference differences between the two models (Plover's flat response to distasteful content, Willet's aversion to harm-adjacent work) don't really come into play. Willet does have a slight edge in self-reported appetite for open-ended generative work, but a structured training deck is more execution-and-accuracy than open-ended invention, and the capability gap favors Plover clearly enough to be the deciding factor.
